title: CAT Vocabulary
note: Words are grouped by meaning, because CAT tests discrimination between near-synonyms far more often than it tests raw recall. Learn each group as a set and note what separates its members.

words.def: to praise highly, especially in public
words.sent: Critics lauded the film for its restraint.

words.def: to praise enthusiastically and at length
words.sent: He extolled the virtues of a slower life.

words.def: to regard with deep respect, often approaching worship
words.sent: The text is venerated by scholars of every school.

words.def: a formal expression of high praise
words.sent: Her retirement drew encomiums from across the industry.

words.def: enthusiastic and public approval
words.sent: The novel met with immediate critical acclaim.

words.def: to express severe and formal disapproval of
words.sent: The committee censured him for the omission.

words.def: to criticise unfairly so as to damage a reputation
words.sent: He never denigrates a rival's work in public.

words.def: to speak or write about in an abusively disparaging way
words.sent: The reformer was vilified in the press for a decade.

words.def: to reprimand severely
words.sent: She castigated the team for missing the deadline.

words.def: to censure or denounce in scathing terms
words.sent: The report excoriates the regulator's inaction.

words.def: a strong verbal or written attack on an opinion
words.sent: The essay is less an argument than a polemic.

words.def: deceitfulness in speech or conduct; double-dealing

words.def: sly or cunning intelligence used to deceive
words.sent: She won the account through patience rather than guile.

words.def: a deceit or trick used to achieve an end

words.def: superficially plausible but in fact wrong

words.def: not candid; pretending to know less than one does

words.def: excessively talkative, especially about trivial matters

words.def: inclined to talk a great deal

words.def: using more words than are needed
words.sent: The contract is verbose where it should be exact.

words.def: tediously lengthy in speech or writing

words.def: high-sounding but with little substance
words.sent: The speech was bombastic and said almost nothing.

words.def: using very few words
words.sent: His laconic reply ended the discussion.

words.def: habitually saying little; reserved by temperament
words.sent: A taciturn man, he spoke only when asked.

words.def: expressed briefly and clearly

words.def: brief, forceful and full of meaning

words.def: unwilling to reveal one's thoughts or feelings

words.def: stubbornly refusing to change an opinion or course

words.def: unwilling to compromise or reach agreement

words.def: obstinately uncooperative toward authority

words.def: hard to control, manage or solve

words.def: refusing to be persuaded or to change one's mind

words.def: ready to accept control or instruction

words.def: excessively obedient or attentive in order to please

words.def: a person who flatters others to gain advantage

words.def: showing respectful submission to another's judgement

words.def: easily provoked to anger

words.def: eager or quick to argue or fight

words.def: hostile and aggressive

words.def: angry and bitter in tone

words.def: to make someone less angry or hostile

words.def: to soften the anger or anxiety of

words.def: an excessive amount of something

words.def: beyond what is required or sufficient

words.def: to waste away, typically from disuse

words.def: to dry out thoroughly

words.def: lasting for a very short time

words.def: lasting or recurring over a long period

words.def: acting with care and thought for the future
